lesson_fields.title: Summation and Series
lesson_fields.summary: Use sigma notation and the standard sum formulas for arithmetic and geometric series.
lesson_fields.summary_fr: Utiliser la notation sigma et les formules classiques de somme des series arithmetiques et geometriques.
lesson_fields.content: A **series** is the sum of the terms of a sequence. **Sigma notation** compresses that sum into one symbol. For an arithmetic series the pairing trick gives `S(n) = n (u(1) + u(n)) / 2`. For a geometric series, `S(n) = u(1)(1 - q^n) / (1 - q)` when `q` is not 1.
lesson_fields.content_fr: Une **serie** est la somme des termes d une suite. La **notation sigma** resume cette somme en un seul symbole. Pour une serie arithmetique, l astuce des extremites donne `S(n) = n (u(1) + u(n)) / 2`. Pour une serie geometrique, `S(n) = u(1)(1 - q^n) / (1 - q)` lorsque `q` est different de 1.
objectives: Apply the sum formula for an arithmetic series
Apply the sum formula for a geometric series
objectives_fr: Appliquer la formule de somme d une serie arithmetique
Appliquer la formule de somme d une serie geometrique

steps.title: Sigma notation
steps.content:
The Greek letter **sigma** `Σ` means "add up". We write the start and end below and above:

    Σ (from k = 1 to n) of u(k)  =  u(1) + u(2) + ... + u(n)

The letter after sigma names the running term, and the two numbers set where the sum starts and stops.

Example:

    Σ (k = 1 to 4) of k  =  1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10
steps.content_fr:
La lettre grecque **sigma** `Σ` signifie "additionner". On ecrit le debut et la fin autour du symbole.

    Σ de k = 1 a n de u(k)  =  u(1) + u(2) + … + u(n)

La lettre apres sigma designe le terme courant ; les bornes indiquent ou commence et ou finit la somme.

Exemple :

    Σ de 1 a 4 de k  =  1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10

steps.title: Sum of an arithmetic series
steps.content:
Pair the first term with the last, the second with the second-to-last. Every pair gives the same total, `u(1) + u(n)`.

There are `n/2` such pairs, so:

    S(n) = n (u(1) + u(n)) / 2

Example, `u(1) = 3`, `r = 4`, `n = 10`:

    u(10) = 3 + 9 x 4 = 39
    S(10) = 10 x (3 + 39) / 2 = 210
steps.content_fr:
Apparie le premier terme avec le dernier, le deuxieme avec l avant-dernier. Chaque paire donne le meme total, `u(1) + u(n)`.

Il y a `n/2` paires de ce type, donc :

    S(n) = n (u(1) + u(n)) / 2

Exemple, `u(1) = 3`, `r = 4`, `n = 10` :

    u(10) = 3 + 9 x 4 = 39
    S(10) = 10 x (3 + 39) / 2 = 210

steps.title: Sum of a geometric series
steps.content:
For a geometric series with ratio `q` different from 1:

    S(n) = u(1) (1 - q^n) / (1 - q)

Example, `u(1) = 2`, `q = 3`, `n = 4`:

    S(4) = 2 (1 - 3^4) / (1 - 3) = 2 (1 - 81) / (-2) = 2 x (-80) / (-2) = 80

Check by adding: 2 + 6 + 18 + 54 = 80.
steps.content_fr:
Pour une serie geometrique de raison `q` differente de 1 :

    S(n) = u(1) (1 - q^n) / (1 - q)

Exemple, `u(1) = 2`, `q = 3`, `n = 4` :

    S(4) = 2 (1 - 3^4) / (1 - 3) = 2 (1 - 81) / (-2) = 2 x (-80) / (-2) = 80

Verification en additionnant : 2 + 6 + 18 + 54 = 80.

steps.title: Choosing the formula
steps.content:
**Arithmetic** (constant difference): `S(n) = n (u(1) + u(n)) / 2`.

**Geometric** (constant ratio, `q` not 1): `S(n) = u(1) (1 - q^n) / (1 - q)`.

Identify the family first, then pick the formula.
steps.content_fr:
**Arithmetique** (difference constante) : `S(n) = n (u(1) + u(n)) / 2`.

**Geometrique** (raison constante, `q` different de 1) : `S(n) = u(1) (1 - q^n) / (1 - q)`.

Identifie d abord la famille, puis choisis la formule.

questions.text: The arithmetic series has u1 = 2 and u(6) = 27. Which formula gives S(6)?
questions.text_fr: La serie arithmetique a u1 = 2 et u(6) = 27. Quelle formule donne S(6) ?

questions.text: What does the symbol Sigma with limits 1 and 4 express?
questions.text_fr: Que represente le symbole Sigma avec les bornes 1 et 4 ?
questions.explanation: Sigma means a sum. The limits 1 to 4 mean you add the expression for each integer from 1 up to 4.
questions.explanation_fr: Sigma signifie une somme. Les bornes de 1 a 4 indiquent que l on ajoute l expression pour chaque entier de 1 a 4.

questions.text: A geometric series has q = 1. Why does the sum formula need a special case?
questions.text_fr: Une serie geometrique a q = 1. Pourquoi la formule de somme a-t-elle besoin d un cas particulier ?
questions.explanation: When q = 1 the denominator 1 - q is zero, so the formula cannot be used. Instead every term equals u(1), so S(n) = n x u(1).
questions.explanation_fr: Lorsque q = 1 le denominateur 1 - q est nul : la formule est inutilisable. Dans ce cas chaque terme vaut u(1), donc S(n) = n x u(1).

choices.text: Because the denominator 1 - q would be zero, and instead S(n) = n x u(1)
choices.text_fr: Parce que le denominateur 1 - q serait nul, et alors S(n) = n x u(1)

choices.text: Because q must always be greater than 1
choices.text_fr: Parce que q doit toujours etre superieur a 1

choices.text: Because the first term becomes zero
choices.text_fr: Parce que le premier terme devient nul

choices.text: Because the series stops being geometric
choices.text_fr: Parce que la serie cesse d etre geometrique
